crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers include application design, integration, performance and hardware/software interaction relevant to mobile engineering, but do not isolate mobile OS lifecycle, device variation or emulator-versus-device evidence.

findings.summary: O*NET Software Developer work provides a broad human-work baseline for mobile application implementation, integration and performance while the AXM package narrows it around mobile lifecycle/device/runtime constraints.
findings.rationale: The candidate body explicitly reconstructs mobile lifecycle, device variation, local/offline state and packaging/update machinery.

findings.summary: Mobile engineering needs an explicit emulator/simulator/physical-device evidence boundary because broad software occupational evidence does not make device/runtime parity claims safe by default.
method_labels: O*NET occupational baseline plus AXM runtime-evidence review
findings.rationale: The reusable package must preserve execution-surface identity so one emulator/device result cannot silently become universal mobile correctness.

gaps_against_body.description: Make emulator, simulator, physical-device and OS-version evidence surfaces explicit and require narrower claims or additional evidence before device/platform parity assertions.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim complete reconstruction of Mobile Application Engineer.
The Software Developer occupation mapping remains partial rather than AXM profession identity.
No device parity, privacy, security, accessibility, platform-policy, TEST, WORKING or CANON claim is created.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This packet grants no platform, privacy, security, product, device, accessibility or institutional authority.
